adventures.name: Bobcat
adventures.summary: Start your Wolf trail! Learn the Scout Oath and Law. Learn the Cub Scout signs.

requirements.adultText: Spend time getting acquainted with the other Scouts in the den.
requirements.kidText: Meet your den friends. Say hi to each one. Learn their names.

params.title: Meet your den
kidSteps: Say hi to each Scout in your den.
Ask each Scout a fun question.
params.parentNote: Approve once your Scout has met the den members and can name them.

requirements.adultText: Say the Oath and the Law out loud, alongside the den and den leader.
requirements.kidText: Say the Scout Oath and Law out loud. Say them with your den. Your leader says them too. Try it here first!

params.title: Say the Oath and Law
params.parentNote: The den leader leads the group while your Scout joins in. A handbook or prompts are fine. Approve after your Scout takes part.

params.prompt: Put the lines of the Scout Oath in order.
steps: On my honor I will do my best
to do my duty to God and my country
and to obey the Scout Law;
to help other people at all times;

lines: The Oath is a promise. The Law is 12 ways to act.
Strong body, ready mind, doing right. That ends the Oath.
Say them with your den. Hold up the Cub Scout sign.
Now put the Oath lines in order. Tap Show me if you forget.

posters.title: Scout Oath
lines: On my honor I will do my best
to do my duty to God and my country
and to obey the Scout Law;
to help other people at all times;
to keep myself physically strong,
mentally awake, and morally straight.

posters.title: Scout Law
lines: A Scout is trustworthy, loyal, helpful,
friendly, courteous, kind,
obedient, cheerful, thrifty,
brave, clean, and reverent.

requirements.notes: Practice is the Oath by line. The Law points are taught in requirement 3.

requirements.adultText: Get to know the twelve points of the Scout Law and what each one asks of a Scout.
requirements.kidText: The Scout Law has 12 points. Each point is a way to be good. Let's learn what some mean!

questions.prompt: How many points are in the Scout Law?
questions.explain: There are 12 points. Scouts try to do all 12.

questions.prompt: Which point means people can believe you?
questions.explain: Trustworthy. You tell the truth and do what you say.

questions.prompt: What does brave mean?
questions.explain: Brave people may feel scared. They still do right.

questions.prompt: Which point means you do not waste things?
questions.explain: Thrifty means you save and use things well.

lines: This is the Scout Law. It has 12 points.
Trustworthy means people can trust you.
Brave means you do right when you are scared.
Thrifty means you save things and do not waste.

posters.title: Scout Law: A Scout is
lines: Trustworthy
Loyal
Helpful
Friendly
Courteous
Kind
Obedient
Cheerful
Thrifty
Brave
Clean
Reverent

requirements.notes: Quiz teaches meanings; the 12 points are not asked in order. Any later Law question can reuse this style.

requirements.adultText: Work with the den to write a short set of behavior rules that everyone agrees to follow.
requirements.kidText: Your den makes a list of rules. It is called a Code of Conduct. Share one good rule. Pick the best ones together.

params.title: Make a den code
params.parentNote: The den leader guides the group to agree on a few simple rules, such as taking turns or being kind. Approve once your Scout has joined in.

params.prompt: Which rules help a den? Sort them.

lines: A den makes rules so everyone can have fun.
Good rules: take turns, listen, be kind, help clean up.
Pushing to be first is not a good rule.
Laughing at mistakes is not a good rule.

requirements.adultText: Perform the Cub Scout sign, salute, and handshake, and show or tell when each one is used.
requirements.kidText: Show the Cub Scout sign, salute, and handshake. Show when you use each one. Learn them here first.

params.title: Sign, salute, handshake
kidSteps: Tell when you use each one.
params.parentNote: Your Scout shows all three, and says when each is used. Typical uses: the sign when saying the Oath and Law, the salute when honoring the flag, the handshake to greet other Scouts. A leader or handbook can model them.

questions.prompt: In the Cub Scout sign, how many fingers are up?
questions.explain: Two fingers go up. Your leader can show you.

questions.prompt: In the salute, the two fingers are...
questions.explain: Together. You hold them up near your head.

questions.prompt: When do you give the Cub Scout salute?
choices: To show respect to the flag
questions.explain: You salute to show respect to the flag.

questions.prompt: The Cub Scout handshake is a way to...
questions.explain: It is a friendly hello to other Scouts.

lines: The Cub Scout sign has two fingers up.
The salute holds those two fingers together, near your head.
You salute to show respect to the flag.
The handshake is a friendly hello to other Scouts.

requirements.notes: Demonstrating is physical, so this is a field mission. The quiz is the in-game rehearsal.

requirements.adultText: Tell the den or family about a moment when the Scout followed the motto 'Do Your Best.'
requirements.kidText: Tell about a time you did your best. Tell your den or your family. It can be big or small.

params.title: Tell your best moment
kidSteps: Think of a time you did your best.
Tell your den or your family.
params.parentNote: Listen to the story. Any real effort counts. Approve once your Scout has shared it.

questions.prompt: What is the Cub Scout motto?
questions.explain: The motto is Do Your Best.

questions.prompt: You try hard but you lose. Did you do your best?
questions.explain: Yes! Trying hard is doing your best.

questions.prompt: Which one shows Do Your Best?
questions.explain: You keep going and try again.

lines: This is the Cub Scout motto.
A motto is a short saying to follow.
Doing your best means trying hard.
You can lose and still do your best!

posters.title: Cub Scout Motto
lines: Do Your Best

requirements.adultText: Back at home, the Scout and a parent or guardian complete the exercises in Scouting America's child-abuse-prevention booklet together.
requirements.kidText: Do the safety pages with your parent.

params.title: Safety pages at home
params.parentNote: Find the booklet 'How to Protect Your Children from Child Abuse: A Parent's Guide' (available from scouting.org). Work through its activities with your Scout at home, then approve here.

requirements.notes: Keep this gentle and private. Do not add game content about the topic; the parent handles it offline.

adventures.name: Paws on the Path
adventures.summary: Go on a nature walk! Pack six hiking things. Spot animals on the trail.

requirements.adultText: Know the six hiking items every Cub Scout carries, and show how each one is used.
requirements.kidText: Meet the Six Essentials. They are six things for a hike. Show what each one does.

params.title: Six Essentials show-and-tell
kidSteps: Tell what you do with it.
params.parentNote: The six are a first-aid kit, a filled water bottle, a flashlight, trail food, sun protection, and a whistle. Check that your Scout can say what each is for, then approve.

params.prompt: Fill your hiking pack with the Six Essentials.

lines: The Six Essentials keep you safe on a hike.
Pack a first-aid kit, full water bottle, and flashlight.
Add trail food, sunscreen, and a whistle.
Video games, skateboards, and pillows stay home.

requirements.adultText: Understand what the buddy system is and why it matters on hikes, then pick the buddy who will go along on the walk.
requirements.kidText: A buddy walks with you. Buddies keep each other safe. Learn the buddy rules. Then pick your buddy!

questions.prompt: What is a buddy for?
questions.explain: Buddies keep each other safe.

questions.prompt: Where is your buddy on a hike?
questions.explain: Your buddy stays close, where you can see them.

questions.prompt: You cannot see your group. What do you do?
choices: Stay here and blow your whistle
questions.explain: Stay where you are. Blow your whistle. They will find you.

lines: A buddy hikes with you to keep you safe.
Stay close. You can always see your buddy.
Feel lost? Stay where you are.
Blow your whistle. Your group will find you.

requirements.notes: Picking the buddy is trivial, so this stays digital. The buddy is used in the requirement 5 walk.

requirements.adultText: Decide which clothes and shoes suit the weather and the trail, and wear them on the walk.
requirements.kidText: Pick clothes and shoes for the weather. Put them on for your walk.

params.title: Dress for the trail
kidSteps: Pick clothes and shoes for it.
params.parentNote: Look for sturdy closed shoes and layers or gear that suit the day's weather. Approve after the walk.

params.prompt: Which clothes are good for a hike? Sort them.

items.label: Rain coat on a rainy day

lines: Check the weather before you go.
Wear strong shoes that cover your feet.
Sun? Wear a hat. Rain? Wear a rain coat.
Cold? Wear warm clothes. No flip-flops or dress shoes.

requirements.adultText: Study the Outdoor Code and the Leave No Trace Principles for Kids, both about taking care of nature.
requirements.kidText: Learn to be kind to nature. Leave No Trace means leave nature as you found it. Sort the good and bad choices.

params.prompt: What should you do outdoors? Sort them.

lines: These are the seven Leave No Trace rules for kids.
Leave No Trace means leave nature as you found it.
Each rule helps keep trails, plants, and animals safe.
Now sort the good and bad choices.

posters.title: Leave No Trace for Kids
lines: Know before you go. Learn about the place first.
Choose the right path. Stay on the trail.
Trash your trash. Take your trash home.
Leave what you find. Rocks and flowers stay.
Be careful with fire. Never leave it alone.
Respect wildlife. Watch animals from far away.
Be kind to other people. Share the trail.

requirements.notes: Items follow the Leave No Trace Principles for Kids (know before you go, choose the right path, trash your trash, leave what you find, be careful with fire, respect wildlife, be kind to other visitors).

requirements.adultText: Join the den, the pack, or family members on a nature walk lasting at least thirty minutes. Be ready to tell about four animals (tame or wild) that could turn up on the trail.
requirements.kidText: Take a walk outside. Walk for 30 minutes. Look for animals. Tell about four you could see.

params.title: Take a nature walk
kidSteps: Go with your den, pack, or family.
Look for animals as you go.
Tell about four animals you could see.
params.parentNote: Walk at least 30 minutes with the den, pack, or family. Your Scout should describe four different animals, pets or wild, that could be seen on the walk, such as how they look and where they live. Approve after the walk.

params.prompt: Find four animals on the nature trail.

lines: Animals live all along the trail. Let's spot four!
Birds sit in the trees. Squirrels have bushy tails.
Rabbits hide in grass and bushes.
Frogs stay near the water.

requirements.notes: Schema allows one practice, so the in-game rehearsal is animal spotting. A navigate walk could be added later.

adventures.name: Running with the Pack
adventures.summary: Taste foods of every color. Brush your teeth. Move your body, and rest too.

requirements.adultText: Taste three foods whose natural colors all differ. Each one should be a protein, veggie, fruit, dairy item, or grain.
requirements.kidText: Taste three foods. Each one is a different color. The colors come from nature.

params.title: Taste the rainbow
kidSteps: Make each one a different color.
params.parentNote: Natural color means not dyed, such as red strawberries, green peas, or orange carrots. Each food should be a protein, vegetable, fruit, dairy, or grain. Approve after the tasting.

params.prompt: Which color is each food? Sort them.

lines: Foods come in many colors. Let's sort some!
Strawberries and tomatoes are red.
Broccoli and peas are green.
Carrots and sweet potatoes are orange.

requirements.adultText: Show a parent or leader how to brush teeth the right way.
requirements.kidText: Show how you brush your teeth. Brush the fronts, backs, and tops. Use a little toothpaste.

params.title: Brush like a pro
kidSteps: Squeeze out a bit the size of a pea.
Brush the fronts, backs, and tops.
params.parentNote: Look for a small amount of toothpaste, every tooth surface brushed, and about two minutes of brushing. Offer gentle tips, then approve.

questions.prompt: How long do you brush your teeth?
questions.explain: Two minutes is just right.

questions.prompt: How much toothpaste do you use?
choices: A bit the size of a pea
questions.explain: A bit the size of a pea is enough.

questions.prompt: Which parts of your teeth do you brush?
questions.explain: Brush every side of every tooth.

lines: Brush your teeth for two minutes.
Use a bit of toothpaste the size of a pea.
Brush the fronts, the backs, and the tops.
Every side of every tooth gets a turn.

requirements.adultText: Keep moving for half an hour alongside the den or one or more other people, mixing in stretching.
requirements.kidText: Move for 30 minutes with friends. Stretch first. Then run, jump, and play!

params.title: Move and stretch
kidSteps: Pick a friend or your den.
Run, jump, or play a game.
params.parentNote: Your Scout is active for 30 minutes with the den or at least one other person, and the time includes stretching and moving. Approve afterward.

params.prompt: Warm up with jumping jacks. Tap to the beat!

lines: Stretch first, so your body is ready.
Then move for 30 minutes with friends.
Let's warm up with jumping jacks!
Tap to the beat, like a drum.

requirements.adultText: Do ten minutes of exercises that the Scout picks personally.
requirements.kidText: Pick your own exercises. Do them for 10 minutes.

params.title: My exercise time
kidSteps: Pick two or three exercises you like.
params.parentNote: Your Scout picks exercises such as squats, sit-ups, or jumping, and does them for ten minutes in total. Offer tips on form, then approve.

params.prompt: Try some squats. Tap to the beat!

lines: Pick exercises you like. Squats are a good one.
Bend your knees low, then stand up tall.
Tap to the beat as you squat.
Do them for 10 minutes. Rest when you need to.

requirements.adultText: Spend ten minutes on a calm, relaxing activity.
requirements.kidText: Do something calm for 10 minutes. Read, draw, or breathe slowly.

params.title: Calm time
kidSteps: Try reading, drawing, or slow breaths.
params.parentNote: Any quiet, relaxing activity works. Approve once your Scout has taken the full ten minutes.

requirements.adultText: Together, review the Scout's yearly health and medical form and discuss which den and pack activities the Scout can join.
requirements.kidText: Look at your health form with your parent. Talk about den and pack fun you can join.

params.title: Health form talk
kidSteps: Look at your health form together.
Talk about den and pack fun you can join.
params.parentNote: Review the Scouting America Annual Health and Medical Record with your Scout, talk about any limits on activities, and share what matters with den leaders. Do not enter health details in this game.

requirements.notes: Never collect health details in the game. This is a parent conversation only.

adventures.name: Council Fire
adventures.summary: Learn to fold the flag. Build your own town. Help your neighbors.

requirements.adultText: Find out how to treat the American flag with respect, practice folding it, and join a flag ceremony with the den or pack.
requirements.kidText: Learn to fold the flag. Treat it with care. Join a flag ceremony. That is when your den shows respect for the flag.

params.title: Care for the flag
kidSteps: Learn how to care for the flag.
Join a flag ceremony with your den or pack.
params.parentNote: A leader or adult shows flag care, such as keeping it off the ground, and your Scout practices the triangle fold with help. Approve after your Scout joins the ceremony.

params.prompt: Put the flag folding steps in order.
steps: Hold the flag flat and off the ground.
Fold it in half the long way.
Fold it in half the long way again.
Start at the striped end. Fold the corner over.
Keep folding the corner over to the end.
Tuck in the end so only stars show.

lines: Hold the flag flat and off the ground.
Fold it in half the long way. Do it twice.
Fold the striped corner over. Keep folding to the end.
Tuck in the end so only stars show.

requirements.adultText: Pick out three Scout Law points that show how to be a good neighbor.
requirements.kidText: Good neighbors are kind and helpful. Which Scout Law points fit? Let's find out!

questions.prompt: A neighbor needs help with bags. Which point fits?
questions.explain: Helpful. You help them carry the bags.

questions.prompt: A new family moves in. You say hello. Which point?
questions.explain: Friendly. You help them feel welcome.

questions.prompt: You say please and thank you. Which point?
questions.explain: Courteous. That means you are polite.

lines: This is the Scout Law. Some points fit good neighbors.
Helpful means you help out, like with heavy bags.
Friendly means you say hi and welcome new people.
Courteous means you are polite, like saying please.

posters.title: Scout Law: A Scout is
lines: Trustworthy
Loyal
Helpful
Friendly
Courteous
Kind
Obedient
Cheerful
Thrifty
Brave
Clean
Reverent

requirements.notes: Any three fitting Scout Law points satisfy the requirement; the quiz covers helpful, friendly, and courteous.

requirements.adultText: Make a model of the Scout's home using a paper template, household items, or building toys.
requirements.kidText: Make a small model of your home. Use paper, boxes, or blocks.

params.title: Build your home model
params.parentNote: Any safe materials work, such as paper, cardboard, or building blocks. Your Scout should build a model that looks like your home. Approve once it is done.

params.prompt: Pick what you need to build a model house.

lines: A model is a small copy of something real.
A cardboard box can be your house.
Use tape, scissors, and markers to build it.
A banana or a rubber duck will not help.

requirements.adultText: Reuse the same kind of materials to make a model of a community building that the Scout visits.
requirements.kidText: Build a place you visit in town. Use the same stuff as your home model.

params.title: Build a town building
kidSteps: Use the same things as before.
params.parentNote: A place such as a library, school, store, or fire station works. Use the same materials as the home model. Approve once the model is built.

params.prompt: Walk through town. Look for a place you could build.

lines: Your town has places you visit.
Follow the tall markers in order.
Stop at the library, school, fire station, and store.
Think: which one would you build?

requirements.adultText: Put the home and building models together to form a neighborhood.
requirements.kidText: Put your two models together. Make a neighborhood!

params.title: Make a neighborhood
kidSteps: Add roads and trees if you like.
params.parentNote: Combine the two models (or models made by the den) into one neighborhood. Paper roads and trees are a nice touch. Approve once it is set up.

lines: A neighborhood is homes and buildings close together.
Use your home model and your town building.
Add paper roads and trees too.
Chips and toy dinosaurs do not fit.

requirements.adultText: Join in a service project, then explain how helping out benefits the neighborhood.
requirements.kidText: Do a service project. That is a job that helps others. Then tell how it helps.

params.title: Help your neighborhood
kidSteps: Tell how it helps your neighborhood.
params.parentNote: Any suitable project works, such as a clean-up, food drive, or helping neighbors. Your Scout should be able to say how it helps. Approve afterward.

questions.prompt: Which one is a service project?
choices: Pick up trash at a park
questions.explain: Service means helping others.

questions.prompt: How does a clean park help?
questions.explain: A clean park is nicer for everyone.

lines: A service project is a job that helps others.
Picking up trash at a park is service.
Games and TV are fun, but not service.
A clean park is nicer for everyone.

adventures.name: Safety in Numbers
adventures.summary: Learn the Protect Yourself Rules. Stay with a buddy. Play it safe.

requirements.adultText: Once a parent or guardian agrees, the Scout views the Wolf version of the 'Protect Yourself Rules' video.
requirements.kidText: Ask your parent if you can watch a safety video. Watch it together.

params.title: Protect Yourself video
kidSteps: Ask your parent to watch with you.
Tell your parent what you learned.
params.parentNote: Preview and watch the Wolf-level 'Protect Yourself Rules' video from Scouting America with your Scout. You decide whether to watch together. Approve once it has been watched.

requirements.adultText: Have a conversation about 'safe touch,' using what the video showed.
requirements.kidText: Talk with your parent about safe touch. Say what you learned.

params.title: Talk about safe touch
kidSteps: Talk with a parent or leader.
Share what you learned from the video.
params.parentNote: Keep it calm and open. Remind your Scout that they can always tell you or another trusted adult if something feels wrong. Approve once you have talked.

questions.prompt: Something feels wrong. What do you do?
questions.explain: Tell a trusted adult. Keep telling until you get help.

questions.prompt: Who is a trusted adult?
choices: A grown-up you know and trust
questions.explain: It is a grown-up you know and your parents trust.

questions.prompt: Can you say no to unsafe touch?
questions.explain: Yes. Your body is yours. Then tell a trusted adult.

lines: A trusted adult is a grown-up you know and trust.
If something feels wrong, tell a trusted adult.
Keep telling until you get help.
Your body is yours. Say no to unsafe touch.

requirements.notes: Practice stays general and gentle. Do not add detail beyond the official Protect Yourself Rules video.

requirements.adultText: Find out about the buddy system, then show how buddies stay together.
requirements.kidText: Learn the buddy system. That means you stay with a buddy. Show how buddies stay together.

params.title: Stay with your buddy
kidSteps: Show how buddies look out for each other.
params.parentNote: Your Scout picks a buddy and shows how buddies stay together, for example on a walk or at play. Approve once you have seen it.

params.prompt: Which ones are the buddy way?

items.label: Stay where you can see your buddy
Tell your buddy where you go

lines: The buddy system means you stay with a buddy.
Stay where you can see your buddy.
Tell your buddy where you go. Check on them.
Never leave your buddy. Never walk off or swim alone.

requirements.adultText: Go over everyday safety rules, then show correct, safe ways to use playground gear such as slides and swings.
requirements.kidText: Learn playground safety rules. Show the safe way to play.

params.title: Playground safety
kidSteps: Go to a playground with an adult.
Show the safe way to use the slide and swings.
params.parentNote: Review simple rules with your Scout and watch them use the equipment safely. Approve afterward.

params.prompt: Which ones are safe at the playground? Sort them.

lines: Wait your turn on the slide and swings.
Slide down feet first.
Sit on the swing seat. Never stand on it.
Never climb up the slide or push anyone.

adventures.name: Footsteps
adventures.summary: Talk about your family's faith. Do something kind. Learn why the truth matters.

requirements.adultText: Discuss your family's faith customs with a parent or guardian, pick three special days or celebrations your family observes, and make art or a craft about the one you like best.
requirements.kidText: Talk with your parent about your family's faith. Name three special days. Make art about your favorite.

params.title: Family faith and art
kidSteps: Talk with your parent about your family's faith.
Name three special days or holidays.
Make art about your favorite one.
params.parentNote: Any faith or belief tradition your family follows counts, and the game never asks which. Approve after the talk and the craft.

requirements.notes: Stay neutral about any faith. A council copy says a religious emblem may be earned in place of this adventure; that note was not confirmed in the official text I could read.

requirements.adultText: Go with family to a religious service or a similar gathering where the family shows respect for what it holds dear.
requirements.kidText: Go to a service or get-together with your family. Notice how your family shows respect.

params.title: Family get-together
kidSteps: Go to a service or get-together with your family.
Notice how your family shows respect.
params.parentNote: A religious service or any gathering that shows how your family expresses reverence counts. Approve afterward.

requirements.adultText: Do something kind for someone.
requirements.kidText: Do one kind thing for someone. Be a helper!

params.title: Do a kind thing
kidSteps: Think of a kind thing to do.
Tell your parent how it felt.
params.parentNote: Any real act of kindness counts. Approve once your Scout has done it.

items.label: Make a card for a sad friend

lines: Being kind means caring how others feel.
Share your toy. Help carry bags. Say thank you.
Make a card for a sad friend.
Laughing at friends or leaving them out is not kind.

requirements.adultText: Hear or read the Aesop tale 'The Boy Who Cried Wolf,' then discuss with the den or family why honesty is valuable.
requirements.kidText: Hear the story of the boy who cried wolf. Talk about why the truth matters.

params.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
kidSteps: Read or listen to the story.
Talk with your den or family.
Say why telling the truth matters.
params.parentNote: Read or listen to Aesop's fable together, then talk about why honesty matters. Approve after the talk.

steps: A boy watches the sheep on a hill.
He yells wolf as a joke.
They find no wolf, and he laughs.
A real wolf comes, and he yells for help.
No one believes him this time.

lines: A boy watches sheep on a hill.
He yells wolf as a joke. People run to help.
No wolf! He laughs. Later, a real wolf comes!
He yells for help, but no one believes him.

requirements.notes: The fable is public domain; the retelling here is original wording.

electives.name: A Wolf Goes Fishing
electives.summary: Learn about fish and bait. Learn to cast. Then go fishing with your family.

electives.name: Adventures in Coins
electives.summary: Look at coins up close. Find the tiny letter that shows where each was made. Play a coin game. Make a rubbing.

electives.name: Air of the Wolf
electives.summary: Fold paper planes and fly them. Which one goes farthest? Then build a new flyer.

electives.name: Champions for Nature
electives.summary: Learn what nature gives us. Use less, use things again, and recycle! Help nature with a project.

electives.name: Code of the Wolf
electives.summary: Make a secret code and send notes. Spot shapes and colors all around you.

electives.name: Computing Wolves
electives.summary: Learn what is inside a computer. Make a story on a computer or tablet. Make safe screen rules.

electives.name: Cubs Who Care
electives.summary: Learn how people see, hear, and move in new ways. Find ways to help everyone join in.

electives.name: Digging in the Past
electives.summary: Learn about dinosaurs! Dig for fossils. Make up your own dinosaur.

electives.name: Finding Your Way
electives.summary: Read maps. Draw a map to your home. Use a compass to find north, east, south, and west.

electives.name: Germs Alive!
electives.summary: Wash up and see how germs spread. Try fun germ tests. Grow some mold!

electives.name: Let's Camp
electives.summary: Get ready for a campout. Learn camp skills. Sleep out with your pack.

electives.name: Paws for Water
electives.summary: Learn swim safety rules. Swim with a buddy. Try a swim stroke.

electives.name: Paws of Skill
electives.summary: Learn to be a good sport. Learn a team game. Cheer on a team.

electives.name: Pedal with the Pack
electives.summary: Wear a helmet the right way. Learn bike hand signals. Ride with your pack.

electives.name: Race Time
electives.summary: Build a small wood race car or a boat. Learn the race rules. Race and be a good sport.

electives.name: Spirit of the Water
electives.summary: Find out where your water comes from. Learn how to keep water clean and save it.

electives.name: Summertime Fun
electives.summary: Go to three Cub Scout events from May to August.

electives.name: Archery
electives.summary: Shoot arrows at a target. Learn the safety rules. You do it at a Scout camp with trained helpers.

electives.name: BB Guns
electives.summary: Learn gun safety rules. Shoot at a target. You do it at a Scout camp with trained helpers.

electives.name: Slingshot
electives.summary: Learn how to stay safe. Shoot at a target. You do it at a Scout camp with trained helpers.
